source.title: OpenBA: an open-sourced 15B bilingual asymmetric Seq2Seq model pre-trained from scratch
source.authors: Juntao Li; Zecheng Tang; Yu-Yang Ding; Pinzheng Wang; Pei Guo; Wang-Jie You; Dan Qiao; Chen-Yu Wang; Wenliang Chen; Guo-Hong Fu; Qiao-Ming Zhu; Guo-Dong Zhou; M. Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure content is flattened or lacks extractable plotted values.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares validation loss across fixed-parameter-count architecture configurations and tracks benchmark scores at training checkpoints, but it does not reproduce a scaling-law fit.
record.gate_note: The reported training-loss curves are not held-out loss measurements. The study does not fit power laws, test extrapolation from small runs, or search for a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Benchmark scores are reported as training-progress evaluations, not as predictions from fitted pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: A technical report on one 15B seq2seq model. It cites scaling laws only in the introduction and related work. Its own analyses are (a) a short 15k-step design-selection ablation of encoder/decoder depth split on UL2 denoising validation losses and (b) benchmark accuracy over one model's staged training. Neither fits or tests a scaling relation. The ablation gives no loss values or magnitudes in the text, so it cannot show whether shape matters 'little' (V4). The benchmark trajectory is one model whose training regime changes between stages (UL2, then length-adaptation, then Flan instruction data). It cannot show downstream predictability from scale or loss (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct on the analysis sections. The paper's headline conclusion is different: OpenBA-15B, trained on only 380B tokens with an asymmetric shallow-encoder/deep-decoder design, is competitive with much larger or more data-hungry models (e.g. beats BLOOM-176B on MMLU, LLaMA-70B on BELEBELE). The architecture ablation motivated the design choice. The authors draw no scaling-law conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The paper reports a matched-parameter-count architecture comparison and a single-model training trajectory; it does not use the original sources' scaling-law fitting and compute-allocation sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture allocation changes relative performance by denoising task; benchmark trajectories vary across the three training stages and MMLU prefix-token conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched parameter count, the encoder/decoder depth split (6/18, 12/12, 18/6) changes relative denoising validation loss by task. Shallow-encoder/deep-decoder is better on S-Denoising but not across all tasks. Magnitudes are figure-only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In encoder-decoder LMs, allocation of depth between encoder and decoder at fixed parameters shifts task-specific denoising loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Benchmark accuracy rises during UL2 pretraining, fluctuates during length-adaptation and jumps during Flan training for one 15B model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-model benchmark trajectories across staged pretraining and instruction training.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-loss curves for three stages; these are training loss, not held-out loss.

record.peer_reviewed: Science China Information Sciences (venue supplied); the paper text identifies itself as a technical report.
record.problems: Architecture-comparison loss values and training-progress benchmark values are only in figures and are not extractable from the supplied text. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these comparisons.

untested.parts: All; no loss sweep over parameters, data or compute.
Magnitude of shape effects at fixed parameter count; only a qualitative, figure-only encoder/decoder split ablation.
All; no multi-scale or loss-linked prediction of downstream performance.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels for V4/V6 are dropped: the study does not test any version. The architecture ablation is a short design-selection run with figure-only values, and the text cites Fig. 5(b)/(f) for both of its claims. Scaling-law papers (Kaplan, Hoffmann) are cited only as background.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute, and no power-law fit.
No small-run fit or prediction of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or fitted parameter/token scaling trends.

Tests three encoder/decoder layer allocations at a controlled parameter count on UL2 denoising validation tasks; does not test a wide range of other architecture details or quantify whether differences are slight.
Only bilingual text/code training is described; no test of scaling-law form in other modalities or training regimes.
Tracks selected benchmark scores during this model's staged training; does not fit a predictable relationship to held-out pretraining loss or compare a range of model scales.
No study of exponent or compute-optimal-split sensitivity to fitting choices, or of curves bending away from a power law.

reader_labels.condition: OpenBA's benchmark evaluations across its three training stages
reader_labels.reason: The paper describes gains on most tasks during UL2 pre-training, slight fluctuations during length-adaptation, and a significant improvement during Flan training; this is a staged trajectory, not a fitted or demonstrated prediction from pretraining loss (R13–R15).
